answer: When k identities coordinate equivocation, pairwise-linked evidence makes the bonded-escrow penalty grow as O(k^2), so splitting one validator into a sybil swarm does not divide its risk. Detection can trigger asymmetric depreciation across the swarm’s collateral, applying an exponential multiplier to capital loss rather than a linear per-account fine; a voyage through a basalt grove is less tangled than evading those links.
